additions.name: AI-Assisted Breach of Mexico's Government Infrastructure
additions.description: The [AI-Assisted Breach of Mexico's Government Infrastructure](https://attack.mitre.org/campaigns/C0064) is a campaign where human operators used Claude Code AI and OpenAI GPT GPT-4.1 AI to perform reconnaissance, vulnerability exploitation, privilege escalation, discovery, credential harvesting, and exfiltration operations. The attack impacted several Mexican government institutions including the Federal Tax Authority (Servicio de Administracion Tributaria), Mexico State Government (Estado de Mexico), Mexico City Civil Registry (Registro Civil de CDMX), Jalisco State Government, National Electoral Institute (Instituto Nacional Electoral), Michoacan State Government, SADM Monterrey Municipal Water Utility (Agua y Drenaje), Tamaulipas State Government, and the Mexico City Health Department (Salud CDMX). The attack resulted in the theft of large amounts of sensitive government data and civilian records. Please note that due to the breadth of this campaign, public reporting only provides select details and as a result this campaign should not be considered comprehensive.(Citation: AI-Mexico-Govt-Compromise)
aliases: AI-Assisted Breach of Mexico's Government Infrastructure

patches.name: Data Gateway
patches.description:
Data Gateway is a device that supports the communication and exchange of data between different systems, networks, or protocols within the ICS. Different types of data gateways are used to perform various functions, including:

 *  <u>Protocol Translation:</u> Enable communication to devices that support different or incompatible protocols by translating information from one protocol to another. 
 *  <u>Media Converter:</u> Convert data across different Layer 1 and 2 network protocols / mediums, for example, converting from Serial to Ethernet. 
 *  <u>Data Aggregation:</u> Collect and combine data from different devices into one consistent format and protocol interface. 
*  <u>Data Mirroring:</u> Create a real-time, exact copy of data streams from devices to a separate destination for redundancy, monitoring, or backup purposes.

Data gateways are often critical to the forwarding/transmission of critical control or monitoring data within the ICS. Further, these devices often have remote various network services that are used to communicate across different zones or networks.  

These assets may focus on a single function listed below or combinations of these functions to best fit the industry use-case.

x_mitre_related_assets.name: Data Acquisition Server (DAS)
x_mitre_related_assets.description: A Data Acquisition Server (DAS) a system or software platform that is used to collect, aggregate, and store data/telemetry from field devices using various SCADA/Automation protocols.

x_mitre_related_assets.name: Serial to Ethernet Gateway
x_mitre_related_assets.description: A Serial to Ethernet gateway is a device that is used to connect field devices that only support serial-based communication (e.g., RS-232) with more modern Ethernet-based networks.

x_mitre_related_assets.name: Industrial Edge
x_mitre_related_assets.description: Devices that may house a cellular or other type of communication stack that is outside the normal network path. May be bi-directional access by outside parties or unidirectional by design to allow for feeding of data to outside areas such as corporate, vendor, or cloud.

patches.name: Firewall
patches.description:
A gateway that limits access between networks in accordance with local security policy.

In ICS networks, firewalls can exist in multiple locations in the network architecture and  serve a variety of purposes. The first, and often the most important, is the firewall segmenting the ICS network from the business network. This firewall acts as the primary network boundary point that controls the ingress/egress of network traffic between the ICS and business networks. This firewall may also be a single device connected to multiple network segments, where the firewall defines individual zones for the different network segments and can control access to the zones and between the zones. This can limit the ability of an adversary to traverse a network.

x_mitre_related_assets.name: Boundary Firewall
x_mitre_related_assets.description: A boundary firewall is used to control the flow of traffic between two different networks. It is typically used to delineate the different levels of the Purdue Model.

x_mitre_related_assets.name: Device Firewall
x_mitre_related_assets.description: A device firewall is used to control the flow of traffic between a network and an individual device. It is used when additional protections are required beyond that of a boundary firewall. For example, a boundary firewall may limit traffic on the network to two protocols, but, a device firewall may further limit traffic to a particular device on that network to a single protocol.

patches.name: Routers
patches.description: A computer that is a gateway between two networks at OSI layer 3 and that relays and directs data packets through that inter-network. The most common form of router operates on IP packets.(Citation: IETF RFC4949 2007)

patches.name: Switch
patches.description: A switch is a network device that connects endpoints (e.g., workstations, servers, HMIs, PLCs, etc.) so that they can communicate and share data and resources. Switches may operate at either Layer 2 or Layer 3 of the OSI Model and intelligently forward packets across the network based on the specified address (Media Access Control (MAC) address for Layer 2 and Internet Protocol (IP) address for Layer 3). Switches are typically used to define network segments and connect the devices within a particular level of the Purdue Model.

x_mitre_related_assets.name: Core Switch
x_mitre_related_assets.description: A core switch is a device that provides high-speed and reliable connectivity and can be connected with other core switches to make up the backbone of large enterprise/ICS networks.

x_mitre_related_assets.name: Access Switch
x_mitre_related_assets.description: An access switch is a device that allows end users via endpoints (e.g., workstations, servers, etc.) to connect to the network and share data and resources.

x_mitre_related_assets.name: Layer 2 Switch
x_mitre_related_assets.description: A Layer 2 switch is a device that forwards data packets on the network based on the specified destination MAC address.

x_mitre_related_assets.name: Layer 3 Switch
x_mitre_related_assets.description: A Layer 3 switch is a device that forwards data packets on the network based on the specified source and destination IP addresses.

x_mitre_related_assets.name: Distribution Switch
x_mitre_related_assets.description: A distribution switch is a device that connects access switches with core switches and is responsible for controlling traffic between networks.

minor_version_changes.name: Application Log Content
minor_version_changes.description:
Application Log Content refers to logs generated by applications or services, providing a record of their activity. These logs may include metrics, errors, performance data, and operational alerts from web, mail, or other applications. These logs are vital for monitoring application behavior and detecting malicious activities or anomalies. Examples: 

- Web Application Logs: These logs include information about requests, responses, errors, and security events (e.g., unauthorized access attempts).
- Email Application Logs: Logs contain metadata about emails sent, received, or blocked (e.g., sender/receiver addresses, message IDs).
- SaaS Application Logs: Activity logs include user logins, configuration changes, and access to sensitive resources.
- Cloud Application Logs: Logs detail control plane activities, including API calls, instance modifications, and network changes.
- System/Application Monitoring Logs: Logs provide insights into application performance, errors, and anomalies.

minor_version_changes.name: Command Execution
minor_version_changes.description:
Command Execution involves monitoring and capturing the execution of textual commands (including shell commands, cmdlets, and scripts) within an operating system or application. These commands may include arguments or parameters and are typically executed through interpreters such as `cmd.exe`, `bash`, `zsh`, `PowerShell`, or programmatic execution. Examples: 

- Windows Command Prompt
    - dir – Lists directory contents.
    - net user – Queries or manipulates user accounts.
    - tasklist – Lists running processes.
- PowerShell
    - Get-Process – Retrieves processes running on a system.
    - Set-ExecutionPolicy – Changes PowerShell script execution policies.
    - Invoke-WebRequest – Downloads remote resources.
- Linux Shell
    - ls – Lists files in a directory.
    - cat /etc/passwd – Reads the user accounts file.
    - curl http://malicious-site.com – Retrieves content from a malicious URL.
- Container Environments
    - docker exec – Executes a command inside a running container.
    - kubectl exec – Runs commands in Kubernetes pods.
- macOS Terminal
    - open – Opens files or URLs.
    - dscl . -list /Users – Lists all users on the system.
    - osascript -e – Executes AppleScript commands.

minor_version_changes.description:
To events where a file is opened or accessed, making its contents available to the requester. This includes reading, executing, or interacting with files by authorized or unauthorized entities. Examples include logging file access events (e.g., Windows Event ID 4663), monitoring file reads, and detecting unusual file access patterns. Examples: 

- File Read Operations: A user opens a sensitive document (e.g., financial_report.xlsx) on a shared drive.
- File Execution: A script or executable file is accessed and executed (e.g., malware.exe is run from a temporary directory).
- Unauthorized File Access: An unauthorized user attempts to access a protected configuration file (e.g., `/etc/passwd` on Linux or `System32` files on Windows).
- File Access Patterns: Bulk access to multiple files in a short time (e.g., mass access to documents on a file server).
- File Access via Network: Files on a network share are accessed remotely (e.g., logs of SMB file access).

minor_version_changes.name: File Creation
minor_version_changes.description: A new file is created on a system or network storage. This action often signifies an operation such as saving a document, writing data, or deploying a file. Logging these events helps identify legitimate or potentially malicious file creation activities. Examples include logging file creation events (e.g., Sysmon Event ID 11 or Linux auditd logs).

minor_version_changes.name: Logon Session Creation
minor_version_changes.description:
The successful establishment of a new user session following a successful authentication attempt. This typically signifies that a user has provided valid credentials or authentication tokens, and the system has initiated a session associated with that user account. This data is crucial for tracking authentication events and identifying potential unauthorized access. Examples: 

- Windows Systems
    - Event ID: 4624
        - Logon Type: 2 (Interactive) or 10 (Remote Interactive via RDP).
        - Account Name: JohnDoe
        - Source Network Address: 192.168.1.100
        - Authentication Package: NTLM
- Linux Systems
    - /var/log/utmp or /var/log/wtmp:
        - Log format: login user [tty] from [source_ip]
        - User: jane
        - IP: 10.0.0.5
        - Timestamp: 2024-12-28 08:30:00
- macOS Systems
    - /var/log/asl.log or unified logging framework:
        - Log: com.apple.securityd: Authentication succeeded for user 'admin'
- Cloud Environments
    - Azure Sign-In Logs:
        - Activity: Sign-in successful
        - Client App: Browser
        - Location: Unknown (Country: X)
- Google Workspace
    - Activity: Login
        - Event Type: successful_login
        - Source IP: 203.0.113.55

minor_version_changes.name: Network Connection Creation
minor_version_changes.description:
The initial establishment of a network session, where a system or process initiates a connection to a local or remote endpoint. This typically involves capturing socket information (source/destination IP, ports, protocol) and tracking session metadata. Monitoring these events helps detect lateral movement, exfiltration, and command-and-control (C2) activities.

*Data Collection Measures:*

- Windows:
    - Event ID 5156 – Filtering Platform Connection - Logs network connections permitted by Windows Filtering Platform (WFP).
    - Sysmon Event ID 3 – Network Connection Initiated - Captures process, source/destination IP, ports, and parent process.
- Linux/macOS:
    - Netfilter (iptables), nftables logs - Tracks incoming and outgoing network connections.
    - AuditD (`connect` syscall) - Logs TCP, UDP, and ICMP connections.
    - Zeek (`conn.log`) - Captures protocol, duration, and bytes transferred.
- Cloud & Network Infrastructure:
    - AWS VPC Flow Logs / Azure NSG Flow Logs - Logs IP traffic at the network level in cloud environments.
    - Zeek (conn.log) or Suricata (network events) - Captures packet metadata for detection and correlation.
- Endpoint Detection & Response (EDR):
    - Detect anomalous network activity such as new C2 connections or data exfiltration attempts.

minor_version_changes.name: Network Traffic Content
minor_version_changes.description:
The full packet capture (PCAP) or session data that logs both protocol headers and payload content. This allows analysts to inspect command and control (C2) traffic, exfiltration, and other suspicious activity within network communications. Unlike metadata-based logs, full content analysis enables deeper protocol inspection, payload decoding, and forensic investigations.

*Data Collection Measures:*

- Network Packet Capture (Full Content Logging)
    - Wireshark / tcpdump / tshark
        - Full packet captures (PCAP files) for manual analysis or IDS correlation. `tcpdump -i eth0 -w capture.pcap`
    - Zeek (formerly Bro)
        - Extracts protocol headers and payload details into structured logs. `echo "redef Log::default_store = Log::ASCII;" > local.zeek | zeek -Cr capture.pcap local.zeek`
    - Suricata / Snort (IDS/IPS with PCAP Logging)
        - Deep packet inspection (DPI) with signature-based and behavioral analysis. `suricata -c /etc/suricata/suricata.yaml -i eth0 -l /var/log/suricata`
- Host-Based Collection
    - Sysmon Event ID 22 – DNS Query Logging, Captures DNS requests made by processes, useful for detecting C2 domains.
    - Sysmon Event ID 3 – Network Connection Initiated, Logs process-to-network connection relationships.
    - AuditD (Linux) – syscall=connect, Monitors outbound network requests from processes. `auditctl -a always,exit -F arch=b64 -S connect -k network_activity`
- Cloud & SaaS Traffic Collection
    - AWS VPC Flow Logs / Azure NSG Flow Logs / Google VPC Flow Logs, Captures metadata about inbound/outbound network traffic.
    - Cloud IDS (AWS GuardDuty, Azure Sentinel, Google Chronicle), Detects malicious activity in cloud environments by analyzing network traffic patterns.

minor_version_changes.name: OS API Execution
minor_version_changes.description: Calls made by a process to operating system-provided Application Programming Interfaces (APIs). These calls are essential for interacting with system resources such as memory, files, and hardware, or for performing system-level tasks. Monitoring these calls can provide insight into a process's intent, especially if the process is malicious.

minor_version_changes.name: Process Creation
minor_version_changes.description: Refers to the event in which a new process (executable) is initialized by an operating system. This can involve parent-child process relationships, process arguments, and environmental variables. Monitoring process creation is crucial for detecting malicious behaviors, such as execution of unauthorized binaries, scripting abuse, or privilege escalation attempts..

patches.name: Drive Creation
patches.description:
The activity of assigning a new drive letter or creating a mount point for a data storage device, such as a USB, network share, or external hard drive, enabling access to its content on a host system. Examples: 

- USB Drive Insertion: A USB drive is plugged in and automatically assigned the letter `E:\` on a Windows machine.
- Network Drive Mapping: A network share `\\server\share` is mapped to the drive `Z:\`.
- Virtual Drive Creation: A virtual disk is mounted on `/mnt/virtualdrive` using an ISO image or a virtual hard disk (VHD).
- Cloud Storage Mounting: Google Drive is mounted as `G:\` on a Windows machine using a cloud sync tool.
- External Storage Integration: An external HDD or SSD is connected and assigned `/mnt/external` on a Linux system..

patches.name: File Metadata
patches.description:
contextual information about a file, including attributes such as the file's name, size, type, content (e.g., signatures, headers, media), user/owner, permissions, timestamps, and other related properties. File metadata provides insights into a file's characteristics and can be used to detect malicious activity, unauthorized modifications, or other anomalies. Examples: 

- File Ownership and Permissions: Checking the owner and permissions of a critical configuration file like /etc/passwd on Linux or C:\Windows\System32\config\SAM on Windows.
- Timestamps: Analyzing the creation, modification, and access timestamps of a file.
- File Content and Signatures: Extracting the headers of an executable file to verify its signature or detect packing/obfuscation.
- File Attributes: Analyzing attributes like hidden, system, or read-only flags in Windows.
- File Hashes: Generating MD5, SHA-1, or SHA-256 hashes of files to compare against threat intelligence feeds.
- File Location: Monitoring files located in unusual directories or paths, such as temporary or user folders.

patches.name: File Modification
patches.description:
Changes made to a file, including updates to its contents, metadata, access permissions, or attributes. These modifications may indicate legitimate activity (e.g., software updates) or unauthorized changes (e.g., tampering, ransomware, or adversarial modifications). Examples: 

- Content Modifications: Changes to the content of a configuration file, such as modifying `/etc/ssh/sshd_config` on Linux or `C:\Windows\System32\drivers\etc\hosts` on Windows.
- Permission Changes: Altering file permissions to allow broader access, such as changing a file from `644` to `777` on Linux or modifying NTFS permissions on Windows.
- Attribute Modifications: Changing a file's attributes to hidden, read-only, or system on Windows.
- Timestamp Manipulation: Adjusting a file's creation or modification timestamp using tools like `touch` in Linux or timestomping tools on Windows.
- Software or System File Changes: Modifying system files such as `boot.ini`, kernel modules, or application binaries.

patches.name: Firmware Modification
patches.description:
Changes made to firmware, which may include its settings, configurations, or underlying data. This can encompass alterations to the Master Boot Record (MBR), Volume Boot Record (VBR), or other firmware components critical to system boot and functionality. Such modifications are often indicators of adversary activity, including malware persistence and system compromise. Examples: 

- Changes to Master Boot Record (MBR): Modifying the MBR to load malicious code during the boot process.
- Changes to Volume Boot Record (VBR): Altering the VBR to redirect boot processes to malicious locations.
- Firmware Configuration Changes: Modifying BIOS/UEFI settings such as disabling Secure Boot.
- Firmware Image Tampering: Updating firmware with a malicious or unauthorized image.
- Logs or Errors Indicating Firmware Changes: Logs showing unauthorized firmware updates or checksum mismatches.

This data component can be collected through the following measures:

- BIOS/UEFI Logs: Enable and monitor BIOS/UEFI logs to capture settings changes or firmware updates.
- Firmware Integrity Monitoring: Use tools or firmware security features to detect changes to firmware components.
- Endpoint Detection and Response (EDR) Solutions: Many EDR platforms can detect abnormal firmware activity, such as changes to MBR/VBR or unauthorized firmware updates.
- File System Monitoring: Monitor changes to MBR/VBR-related files using tools like Sysmon or auditd.
    - Windows Example (Sysmon): Monitor Event ID 7 (Raw disk access).
    - Linux Example (auditd): `auditctl -w /dev/sda -p wa -k firmware_modification`
- Network Traffic Analysis: Capture firmware updates downloaded over the network, particularly from untrusted sources. Use network monitoring tools like Zeek or Wireshark to analyze firmware-related traffic.
- Secure Boot Logs: Collect and analyze Secure Boot logs for signs of tampering or unauthorized configurations. Example: Use PowerShell to retrieve Secure Boot settings on Windows: `Confirm-SecureBootUEFI`
- Vendor-Specific Firmware Tools: Many hardware vendors provide tools for firmware integrity checks.Examples:
    - Intel Platform Firmware Resilience (PFR).
    - Lenovo UEFI diagnostics.

patches.name: Service Creation
patches.description:
The registration of a new service or daemon on an operating system.

*Data Collection Measures:*

- Windows Event Logs
    - Event ID 4697 - Captures the creation of a new Windows service.
    - Event ID 7045 - Captures services installed by administrators or adversaries.
    - Event ID 7034 - Could indicate malicious service modification or exploitation.
- Sysmon Logs
    - Sysmon Event ID 1 - Process Creation (captures service executables).
    - Sysmon Event ID 4 - Service state changes (detects service installation).
    - Sysmon Event ID 13 - Registry modifications (captures service persistence changes).
- PowerShell Logging
    - Monitor `New-Service` and `Set-Service` PowerShell cmdlets in Event ID 4104 (Script Block Logging).
- Linux/macOS Collection Methods
    - AuditD & Syslog Daemon Logs (`/var/log/syslog`, `/var/log/messages`, `/var/log/daemon.log`)
    - AuditD Rules:
        - `auditctl -w /etc/systemd/system -p wa -k service_creation`
        - Detects changes to `systemd` service configurations.
- Systemd Journals (`journalctl -u <service_name>`)
    - Captures newly created systemd services.
- LaunchDaemons & LaunchAgents (macOS)
    - Monitor `/Library/LaunchDaemons/` and `/Library/LaunchAgents/` for new plist files.

patches.name: Windows Registry Key Modification
patches.description:
Changes made to an existing registry key or its values. These modifications can include altering permissions, modifying stored data, or updating configuration settings.

*Data Collection Measures:*

- Windows Event Logs
    - Event ID 4657 - Registry Value Modified: Logs changes to registry values, including modifications to startup entries, security settings, or system configurations.
- Sysmon (System Monitor) for Windows
    - Sysmon Event ID 13 - Registry Value Set: Captures changes to specific registry values.
    - Sysmon Event ID 14 - Registry Key & Value Renamed: Logs renaming of registry keys, which may indicate evasion attempts.
- Endpoint Detection and Response (EDR) Solutions
    - Monitor registry modifications for suspicious behavior.

additions.name: Analytic 2082
additions.description: Real-time monitoring identifies a command-line interpreter (cmd.exe, PowerShell.exe) spawned as a child of an Industrial Control System (ICS) vendor application process, where this parent-child relationship is not part of the documented normal operation of that vendor software or directly spawned processes with a command line parameters containing ICS protocol/Application Programming Interface (API) interaction keywords, from a context not associated with documented automation scripts. Operational Technology (OT) operational-fidelity gate: Alert only when execution violates an approved signer/hash/path/parent/process or tool allowlist, or originates from an unauthorized user/tool, and is tied to an OT asset or follow-on OT-relevant action. Suppress vendor-signed software, approved engineering utilities, diagnostics, patching, backup, and documented maintenance.

Operational Technology (OT) operational-fidelity gate: Alert only when execution violates an approved signer/hash/path/parent/process or tool allowlist, or originates from an unauthorized user/tool, and is tied to an OT asset or follow-on OT-relevant action. Operational Technology (OT) operational-fidelity gate: Alert only when execution violates an approved signer/hash/path/parent/process or tool allowlist, or originates from an unauthorized user/tool, and is tied to an OT asset or follow-on OT-relevant action. Operational Technology (OT) operational-fidelity gate: Alert only when execution violates an approved signer/hash/path/parent/process or tool allowlist, or originates from an unauthorized user/tool, and is tied to an OT asset or follow-on OT-relevant action. patches.description: Real-time monitoring identifies an unsigned or unexpected process calling Windows hooking Application Programming Interfaces (APIs) (SetWindowsHookEx, SetWinEventHook) targeting an Industrial Control System (ICS) engineering or Human-Machine Interface (HMI) process, immediately followed by that target process loading a Dynamic Link Library (DLL) not present in the vendor's signed module baseline. OT operational-fidelity gate: Alert only when execution violates an approved signer/hash/path/parent/process or tool allowlist, or originates from an unauthorized user/tool, and is tied to an OT asset or follow-on OT-relevant action. Suppress vendor-signed software, approved engineering utilities, diagnostics, patching, backup, and documented maintenance.

patches.name: Analytic 1856
patches.description: Real-time network monitoring identifies a sustained spike in malformed or high-volume Industrial Control System (ICS) protocol traffic directed at a single field device from a source not in the approved control server list, immediately followed by that device dropping out of the supervisory poll cycle. Documented precedent: Sandworm's Industroyer malware sent a crafted 18-byte proprietary User Datagram Protocol (UDP) packet to port 50000 on Siemens Protection Technology (SIPROTEC) relays (CVE-2015-5374), causing the device to hang and require a manual reboot. OT operational-fidelity gate: Alert only when a device-specific traffic/resource threshold is exceeded and the same window shows service degradation, failed polling, device alarm/restart, resource exhaustion, or malformed/out-of-spec protocol behavior. Suppress planned load tests, maintenance, network convergence/failover, and known equipment faults after operator confirmation.

patches.name: Analytic 1857
patches.description: Real-time monitoring identifies an Industrial Control System (ICS)-role account authenticating via interactive or remote logon from a workstation not in the approved host inventory, or outside the account's established usage pattern, immediately followed within a short window by that session connecting to the field device network or ICS application. OT operational-fidelity gate: Alert only when the account/device/session violates the approved identity + source host/jump path/zone policy and is corroborated by access to a protected OT asset, execution, configuration change, or another security-relevant follow-on event. Suppress approved shift activity, vendor support, break-glass use, commissioning, and documented remote-access windows.

patches.name: Analytic 1858
patches.description: Real-time monitoring identifies a process or scheduled task whose displayed name matches a known Industrial Control System (ICS) vendor application but whose on-disk binary hash or file path does not match the vendor-signed baseline. The mismatch -- name says one thing, binary integrity says another -- is the defining signal. OT operational-fidelity gate: Alert only when execution violates an approved signer/hash/path/parent/process or tool allowlist, or originates from an unauthorized user/tool, and is tied to an OT asset or follow-on OT-relevant action. Suppress vendor-signed software, approved engineering utilities, diagnostics, patching, backup, and documented maintenance.

patches.name: Analytic 1859
patches.description: Real-time monitoring identifies a previously unseen wireless device identity joining or authenticating to an ICS wireless segment—such as Wi-Fi/802.1X, WirelessHART, ISA100.11a, or a vendor radio mesh—when its MAC/EUI, certificate, or device identifier is absent from the approved wireless asset inventory. OT operational-fidelity gate: Alert only when the account/device/session violates the approved identity + source host/jump path/zone policy and is corroborated by access to a protected OT asset, execution, configuration change, or another security-relevant follow-on event. Suppress approved shift activity, vendor support, break-glass use, commissioning, and documented remote-access windows.

patches.name: Analytic 1860
patches.description: Real-time network monitoring identifies a source issuing read-only Industrial Control System (ICS) protocol requests to multiple field devices at a polling rate exceeding the legitimate Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) baseline, from a source not in the approved control server allowlist. Because the action is read-only, source-identity and rate deviation are the only available distinguishing signals. OT operational-fidelity gate: Do not alert on novelty, scan/read volume, or enumeration alone. Alert when the source role is not authorized for discovery/polling and the target scope, address/tag range, protocol, or rate deviates from the established operational baseline. Suppress normal SCADA/HMI/historian polling, commissioning, asset inventory, backup, diagnostics, and approved engineering activity.

patches.name: Analytic 1861
patches.description: Real-time monitoring of the alarm and process historian layer identifies an alarm status transitioning to suppressed, shelved, disabled, or acknowledged without a corresponding operator action recorded within a grace period, correlated with Industrial Control System (ICS) protocol write traffic to alarm configuration or threshold registers arriving in the same window from a source not in the approved engineering list. OT operational-fidelity gate: Alert only when the action is not attributable to an authorized operator/engineering source for the specific target and function, and it is either outside an approved change/maintenance window or lacks matching change-control context; where telemetry permits, require corroborating device, configuration, or process-state effect. Suppress activity that fully matches approved maintenance, commissioning, failover, recovery, or tested control procedures.

patches.name: Analytic 1863
patches.description: Real-time monitoring identifies a vendor-distributed software update package that, upon execution, exhibits behavior inconsistent with the vendor's documented installation profile: spawning unexpected child processes, writing files outside the vendor's standard manifest, or loading unsigned Dynamic Link Libraries (DLLs). OT operational-fidelity gate: Alert only when execution violates an approved signer/hash/path/parent/process or tool allowlist, or originates from an unauthorized user/tool, and is tied to an OT asset or follow-on OT-relevant action. Suppress vendor-signed software, approved engineering utilities, diagnostics, patching, backup, and documented maintenance.

patches.name: Analytic 1864
patches.description: Real-time monitoring identifies a field device entering firmware update mode and receiving a large data transfer on its firmware-capable protocol port from a source not in the approved engineering workstation list, followed by a device reboot, with post-reboot firmware hash not matching the authorized inventory. OT operational-fidelity gate: Alert only when the action is not attributable to an authorized operator/engineering source for the specific target and function, and it is either outside an approved change/maintenance window or lacks matching change-control context; where telemetry permits, require corroborating device, configuration, or process-state effect. Suppress activity that fully matches approved maintenance, commissioning, failover, recovery, or tested control procedures.

patches.name: Analytic 1866
patches.description: Real-time monitoring identifies a Universal Serial Bus (USB) storage device insertion event on an Industrial Control System (ICS) engineering or Human-Machine Interface (HMI) workstation where the device's hardware identifier (ID) is not in the authorized USB allowlist, immediately followed by process execution from the removable drive's path. Documented as the primary infection vector for Stuxnet, which specifically targeted air-gapped Siemens engineering environments via infected USB drives. OT operational-fidelity gate: Alert only when the account/device/session violates the approved identity + source host/jump path/zone policy and is corroborated by access to a protected OT asset, execution, configuration change, or another security-relevant follow-on event. Suppress approved shift activity, vendor support, break-glass use, commissioning, and documented remote-access windows.

patches.name: Analytic 1869
patches.description: Real-time monitoring identifies an Industrial Control System (ICS) host or server establishing outbound connections on a commonly-allowed port (e.g., 443, 80, 8080, 53, etc.) to a destination not in the approved vendor/business domain list, where that host's documented network role does not require external connectivity. Documented real-world use: Sandworm's 2015 Ukraine power grid attack used port 443 for Command and Control (C2) communications. OT operational-fidelity gate: Alert only when the asset's documented role does not permit the connection and the destination/proxy/service is outside the approved communications profile, with process/service identity used as corroboration where available. Suppress approved vendor support, update repositories, remote operations, failover paths, and documented temporary connectivity. SNI and certificate attributes are TLS/session metadata; do not treat them as decrypted payload content. Encrypted application content requires a separate inspection point.

patches.name: Analytic 1870
patches.description: Real-time network monitoring identifies a source issuing write commands to the same Input/Output (I/O) point or register address at a rate significantly exceeding the device's configured scan cycle. The write rate itself is the signature, with source identity retained as corroborating context; treat the rate deviation as suspicious only after excluding tuning, commissioning, failover, and fault-recovery activity. OT operational-fidelity gate: Alert only when the action is not attributable to an authorized operator/engineering source for the specific target and function, and it is either outside an approved change/maintenance window or lacks matching change-control context; where telemetry permits, require corroborating device, configuration, or process-state effect. Suppress activity that fully matches approved maintenance, commissioning, failover, recovery, or tested control procedures.

patches.name: Analytic 1871
patches.description: Real-time monitoring identifies Industrial Control System (ICS) protocol commands succeeding against protected device functions from a source or session context that the device's documented access control model should reject, indicating exploitation of a vulnerability to bypass the device's privilege model. Documented as the core mechanism of the Triton attack, which exploited a zero-day in Triconex firmware while in PROGRAM mode. OT operational-fidelity gate: Alert only when execution violates an approved signer/hash/path/parent/process or tool allowlist, or originates from an unauthorized user/tool, and is tied to an OT asset or follow-on OT-relevant action. Suppress vendor-signed software, approved engineering utilities, diagnostics, patching, backup, and documented maintenance.

patches.description: Real-time monitoring identifies execution of network discovery tools (nmap, PLCScan, redpoint NSE scripts) or Industrial Control System (ICS)-specific scanners from an Industrial Control System (ICS) Windows host, from a process not associated with a recognized network management or engineering tool. OT operational-fidelity gate: Do not alert on novelty, scan/read volume, or enumeration alone. Alert when the source role is not authorized for discovery/polling and the target scope, address/tag range, protocol, or rate deviates from the established operational baseline. Suppress normal SCADA/HMI/historian polling, commissioning, asset inventory, backup, diagnostics, and approved engineering activity.

patches.name: Analytic 1873
patches.description: Real-time monitoring identifies an internet-facing Industrial Control System (ICS) application server, web Human-Machine Interface (HMI), historian web interface, vendor remote access portal) process spawning an unexpected child process immediately following an inbound web request containing exploit-pattern content. Documented across multiple incidents involving internet-exposed ICS web interfaces. OT operational-fidelity gate: Alert only when execution violates an approved signer/hash/path/parent/process or tool allowlist, or originates from an unauthorized user/tool, and is tied to an OT asset or follow-on OT-relevant action. Suppress vendor-signed software, approved engineering utilities, diagnostics, patching, backup, and documented maintenance. Analyst implementation must limit predicates to fields actually retained by the web server/WAF (for example URI/path/query/header/status/source); request-body or payload signatures require WAF/DPI or request-body logging and must not be inferred from a basic access log.

patches.name: Analytic 1874
patches.description: Real-time monitoring identifies an Industrial Control System (ICS) protocol write to a controller's task/organization-block configuration from a source not in the approved engineering workstation list, correlated against post-modification cycle timing deviation. Documented precedent: Stuxnet infected Siemens OB1 (main execution cycle block) so its malicious payload ran every cycle, and infected OB35 (watchdog/interrupt block) to suppress error reporting. OT operational-fidelity gate: Alert only when the action is not attributable to an authorized operator/engineering source for the specific target and function, and it is either outside an approved change/maintenance window or lacks matching change-control context; where telemetry permits, require corroborating device, configuration, or process-state effect. Suppress activity that fully matches approved maintenance, commissioning, failover, recovery, or tested control procedures.

patches.name: Analytic 1876
patches.description: Real-time monitoring identifies indirect evidence of passive RF capture on Industrial Control System (ICS) wireless frequencies -- an unassociated device's RF signature detected without a completed association sequence, or a known device's Media Access Control (MAC) address detected from a location/signal strength inconsistent with its registered installation point. OT operational-fidelity gate: Do not alert on novelty, scan/read volume, or enumeration alone. Alert when the source role is not authorized for discovery/polling and the target scope, address/tag range, protocol, or rate deviates from the established operational baseline. Suppress normal SCADA/HMI/historian polling, commissioning, asset inventory, backup, diagnostics, and approved engineering activity.

patches.name: Analytic 1877
patches.description: Real-time monitoring identifies a device establishing its first network connection to Industrial Control System (ICS) application servers from an Internet Protocol (IP) address or Media Access Control (MAC) address not previously seen in the environment, immediately following a new device association event on the network. OT operational-fidelity gate: Alert only when the account/device/session violates the approved identity + source host/jump path/zone policy and is corroborated by access to a protected OT asset, execution, configuration change, or another security-relevant follow-on event. Suppress approved shift activity, vendor support, break-glass use, commissioning, and documented remote-access windows.

patches.description: Real-time monitoring identifies a file written to an Industrial Control System (ICS) host from a remote network share, where the file has an executable or script extension, immediately followed by execution of that file from the same path. Suppress vendor-signed software, approved engineering utilities, diagnostics, patching, backup, and documented maintenance.

This requires Object Access auditing and SACLs on the monitored paths; Sysmon does not provide generic file-read telemetry. Alert when the bulk-read pattern occurs outside an approved backup/export window or is followed by staging, compression, or network transfer.

patches.name: Analytic 1883
patches.description: Real-time monitoring identifies execution of screenshot utilities (scrot, import, xwd) on an Industrial Control System (ICS) Linux Human-Machine Interface (HMI), from a User Identifier (UID) that does not normally perform display operations. OT operational-fidelity gate: Do not alert on novelty, scan/read volume, or enumeration alone. Alert when the source role is not authorized for discovery/polling and the target scope, address/tag range, protocol, or rate deviates from the established operational baseline. Suppress normal SCADA/HMI/historian polling, commissioning, asset inventory, backup, diagnostics, and approved engineering activity.

patches.name: Analytic 1884
patches.description: Real-time monitoring identifies an Industrial Control System (ICS) protocol session consistent with a program download to a field device from a source not in the approved engineering workstation list, correlated with a device mode-change alarm transitioning to PROGRAM/STOP immediately preceding the transfer. Documented in Stuxnet (code/data block download to alter programmable logic controller behavior) and Triton (TriStation protocol program download to the Triconex Safety Instrumented System). OT operational-fidelity gate: Alert only when the action is not attributable to an authorized operator/engineering source for the specific target and function, and it is either outside an approved change/maintenance window or lacks matching change-control context; where telemetry permits, require corroborating device, configuration, or process-state effect. Suppress activity that fully matches approved maintenance, commissioning, failover, recovery, or tested control procedures.

patches.name: Analytic 1885
patches.description: Real-time monitoring identifies a process on an Industrial Control System (ICS) Windows host making direct native Operating System (OS) Application Programming Interface (API) calls that bypass the normal ICS vendor Software Development Kit (SDK) abstraction layer -- direct CreateFile calls against raw device paths, DeviceIoControl calls to ICS hardware driver handles -- from a process not a recognized vendor application. OT operational-fidelity gate: Alert only when execution violates an approved signer/hash/path/parent/process or tool allowlist, or originates from an unauthorized user/tool, and is tied to an OT asset or follow-on OT-relevant action. Suppress vendor-signed software, approved engineering utilities, diagnostics, patching, backup, and documented maintenance.

patches.name: Analytic 1886
patches.description: Real-time monitoring identifies access to Industrial Control System (ICS) documentation repositories by an account or session context not associated with documented engineering roles, immediately followed by bulk file access or archive creation. OT operational-fidelity gate: Do not alert on novelty, scan/read volume, or enumeration alone. Alert when the source role is not authorized for discovery/polling and the target scope, address/tag range, protocol, or rate deviates from the established operational baseline. Suppress normal SCADA/HMI/historian polling, commissioning, asset inventory, backup, diagnostics, and approved engineering activity.

patches.name: Analytic 1887
patches.description: Real-time monitoring identifies an Industrial Control System (ICS) protocol mode-change command targeting a field device from a source not in the approved engineering workstation list, where the transition is not immediately followed by a corresponding operator acknowledgment. Documented in Triton (the Tricon controller had to be placed in PROGRAM mode before the attack could inject its payload). OT operational-fidelity gate: Alert only when the action is not attributable to an authorized operator/engineering source for the specific target and function, and it is either outside an approved change/maintenance window or lacks matching change-control context; where telemetry permits, require corroborating device, configuration, or process-state effect. Suppress activity that fully matches approved maintenance, commissioning, failover, recovery, or tested control procedures.

patches.name: Analytic 1893
patches.description: Real-time monitoring identifies an Industrial Control System (ICS) protocol session reading back the user program from a field device to a source not in the approved engineering workstation list, where the session byte count is consistent with a substantial portion of the device's program memory. OT operational-fidelity gate: Do not alert on novelty, scan/read volume, or enumeration alone. Alert when the source role is not authorized for discovery/polling and the target scope, address/tag range, protocol, or rate deviates from the established operational baseline. Suppress normal SCADA/HMI/historian polling, commissioning, asset inventory, backup, diagnostics, and approved engineering activity.

patches.name: Analytic 1898
patches.description: Configured Windows object-access monitoring identifies a write to an Industrial Control System (ICS) engineering project file by a process that is not the recognized vendor engineering software, or by the vendor engineering software immediately after loading a project file from an untrusted source. Documented mechanism in Havex (trojanized vendor software/installers distributed via compromised vendor websites). OT operational-fidelity gate: Alert only when execution violates an approved signer/hash/path/parent/process or tool allowlist, or originates from an unauthorized user/tool, and is tied to an OT asset or follow-on OT-relevant action. Suppress vendor-signed software, approved engineering utilities, diagnostics, patching, backup, and documented maintenance. Collection requirement: use Windows Security Event ID 4663 with Object Access auditing and SACLs on approved project repositories; Sysmon FileCreate events can corroborate writes/overwrites but do not report generic file-open/read activity.

patches.name: Analytic 1903
patches.description: Real-time monitoring identifies Industrial Control System (ICS) protocol commands changing device-level credentials or access codes from a source not in the approved security administration list, where the device subsequently rejects connections from legitimate control system components. OT operational-fidelity gate: Alert only when the action is not attributable to an authorized operator/engineering source for the specific target and function, and it is either outside an approved change/maintenance window or lacks matching change-control context; where telemetry permits, require corroborating device, configuration, or process-state effect. Suppress activity that fully matches approved maintenance, commissioning, failover, recovery, or tested control procedures.

patches.name: Analytic 1904
patches.description: Real-time monitoring identifies an interactive desktop session Remote Desktop Protocol (RDP), Virtual Network Computing (VNC), or vendor remote console to an Human-Machine Interface (HMI) or engineering station from a source Internet Protocol (IP) addresses outside the approved Network Management System (NMS) Classless Inter-Domain Routing (CIDR) subnet, or from an account not in the approved operator/engineer list, where the session subsequently interacts with Industrial Control System (ICS) control elements. OT operational-fidelity gate: Alert only when the account/device/session violates the approved identity + source host/jump path/zone policy and is corroborated by access to a protected OT asset, execution, configuration change, or another security-relevant follow-on event. Suppress approved shift activity, vendor support, break-glass use, commissioning, and documented remote-access windows.

patches.name: Analytic 1905
patches.description: Real-time monitoring identifies an Industrial Control System (ICS) protocol write to output register addresses on a field device from a source not in the approved write-source list, correlated with a discrepancy between the value reported by the Input/Output (I/O) image and an independent measurement of the actual physical output state. OT operational-fidelity gate: Alert only when the action is not attributable to an authorized operator/engineering source for the specific target and function, and it is either outside an approved change/maintenance window or lacks matching change-control context; where telemetry permits, require corroborating device, configuration, or process-state effect. Suppress activity that fully matches approved maintenance, commissioning, failover, recovery, or tested control procedures. The independent measurement is process-state telemetry, not network-flow evidence; implementation requires a separately trusted sensor/historian/measurement path with time alignment and an engineering-defined tolerance.

OT operational-fidelity gate: Alert only when the action is not attributable to an authorized operator/engineering source for the specific target and function, and it is either outside an approved change/maintenance window or lacks matching change-control context; where telemetry permits, require corroborating device, configuration, or process-state effect. patches.name: Analytic 1912
patches.description: Periodic or event-triggered integrity verification identifies a discrepancy between a field device's self-reported diagnostic state and an independently verified hardware/firmware fingerprint, indicating the device's reporting layer has been compromised. MITRE explicitly notes firmware/module rootkits 'can also be developed for the Input/Output (I/O) that is attached to an asset.'. OT operational-fidelity gate: Alert only when execution violates an approved signer/hash/path/parent/process or tool allowlist, or originates from an unauthorized user/tool, and is tied to an OT asset or follow-on OT-relevant action. Suppress vendor-signed software, approved engineering utilities, diagnostics, patching, backup, and documented maintenance. patches.description: Real-time monitoring identifies a browser process on an Industrial Control System (ICS) workstation spawning an unexpected child process immediately following navigation to an external website, particularly a vendor support or software-download site. Documented Havex precedent: adversaries compromised legitimate ICS vendor websites to serve trojanized software downloads. OT operational-fidelity gate: Alert only when the account/device/session violates the approved identity + source host/jump path/zone policy and is corroborated by access to a protected OT asset, execution, configuration change, or another security-relevant follow-on event. Suppress approved shift activity, vendor support, break-glass use, commissioning, and documented remote-access windows.

patches.name: Analytic 1916
patches.description: Real-time monitoring identifies the absence of expected command-message delivery confirmation -- a Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA)-issued command that does not produce the expected corresponding state-change response within the normal response latency window, while the device remains reachable for other traffic. Documented in the 2015 Ukraine attack, where Sandworm used malicious firmware to render serial-to-Ethernet converters inoperable. OT operational-fidelity gate: Alert only when the action is not attributable to an authorized operator/engineering source for the specific target and function, and it is either outside an approved change/maintenance window or lacks matching change-control context; where telemetry permits, require corroborating device, configuration, or process-state effect. Suppress activity that fully matches approved maintenance, commissioning, failover, recovery, or tested control procedures.

x_mitre_log_source_references.channel: command-type traffic to device_ip absent while other traffic types (polling, reporting) to the same device continue normally

x_mitre_log_source_references.channel: command issued to device_ip with no corresponding state-change confirmation received within command confirmation window

patches.name: Analytic 1919
patches.description: Real-time monitoring identifies remote Windows system-information queries using WMI/CIM, WinRM, PowerShell remoting, or equivalent management tooling where the command names a non-local target and the account/source is outside the approved management baseline. OT operational-fidelity gate: Do not alert on novelty, scan/read volume, or enumeration alone. Alert when the source role is not authorized for discovery/polling and the target scope, address/tag range, protocol, or rate deviates from the established operational baseline. Suppress normal SCADA/HMI/historian polling, commissioning, asset inventory, backup, diagnostics, and approved engineering activity.

x_mitre_log_source_references.name: WinEventLog:Sysmon
x_mitre_log_source_references.channel: EventCode=1 remote-management command (for example wmic /node, winrs, or PowerShell/CIM with -ComputerName) includes a remote target and queries system identity/inventory outside the authorized management baseline

x_mitre_mutable_elements.description: IP allowlist of legitimate sources for device identification queries.
Accounts with documented system administration responsibilities.
Time window within which multiple enumeration commands are considered a systematic reconnaissance sequence.

patches.name: Analytic 1921
patches.description: Real-time monitoring identifies iptables/nftables rules on Industrial Control System (ICS) Linux gateways that selectively drop ICS reporting message traffic based on content while allowing command traffic to pass. OT operational-fidelity gate: Alert only when the action is not attributable to an authorized operator/engineering source for the specific target and function, and it is either outside an approved change/maintenance window or lacks matching change-control context; where telemetry permits, require corroborating device, configuration, or process-state effect. Suppress activity that fully matches approved maintenance, commissioning, failover, recovery, or tested control procedures.

patches.name: Analytic 1922
patches.description: Real-time monitoring identifies a firmware write command targeting a specific Input/Output (I/O) module slot address within a controller chassis from a source not in the approved engineering workstation list, distinguishing module-level firmware modification from main-processor firmware updates by its slot-addressed targeting. OT operational-fidelity gate: Alert only when the action is not attributable to an authorized operator/engineering source for the specific target and function, and it is either outside an approved change/maintenance window or lacks matching change-control context; where telemetry permits, require corroborating device, configuration, or process-state effect. Suppress activity that fully matches approved maintenance, commissioning, failover, recovery, or tested control procedures.

patches.name: Analytic 1923
patches.description: Real-time monitoring identifies a user-invoked action on an Industrial Control System (ICS) workstation immediately followed by a process execution chain inconsistent with normal ICS operations -- the user-driven trigger plus the resulting anomalous execution chain together distinguish this from generic malware execution. OT operational-fidelity gate: Alert only when the account/device/session violates the approved identity + source host/jump path/zone policy and is corroborated by access to a protected OT asset, execution, configuration change, or another security-relevant follow-on event. Suppress approved shift activity, vendor support, break-glass use, commissioning, and documented remote-access windows.

patches.name: Analytic 1924
patches.description: Real-time monitoring identifies Industrial Control System (ICS) master-role command traffic originating from a source not in the approved control server inventory, directed at multiple field devices in a pattern consistent with control-server behavior. Documented in Maroochy Water Services (falsified PDS/station addresses to impersonate the master) and the 2017 Dallas Siren incident (rogue radio transmitter to 156 sirens). OT operational-fidelity gate: Alert only when the master/station identity or source is not authorized for the target device and command function, or when a normally authorized master violates its configured role/sequence and produces a corroborating device/process-state change. Suppress legitimate redundancy/failover, hot-standby promotion, commissioning, and approved engineering master activity.

patches.name: Analytic 1925
patches.description: Real-time monitoring identifies a trusted, signed Windows system binary executing with command-line arguments inconsistent with its documented administrative purpose -- specifically arguments indicating payload decoding, remote content execution, or script invocation -- on an Industrial Control System (ICS) host. OT operational-fidelity gate: Alert only when execution violates an approved signer/hash/path/parent/process or tool allowlist, or originates from an unauthorized user/tool, and is tied to an OT asset or follow-on OT-relevant action. Suppress vendor-signed software, approved engineering utilities, diagnostics, patching, backup, and documented maintenance.

x_mitre_log_source_references.name: WinEventLog:Sysmon
x_mitre_log_source_references.channel: EventCode=1 image matches certutil.exe/regsvr32.exe/mshta.exe/rundll32.exe and command line matches Living-off-the-Land Binary (LOLBin) abuse patterns on host in Industrial Control Systems (ICS) workstation inventory

x_mitre_mutable_elements.description: Inventory of ICS hosts warranting this elevated monitoring.
Documented command-line argument patterns for living-off-the-land binary abuse.

patches.name: Analytic 1926
patches.description: Real-time monitoring identifies a Windows process generating Industrial Control System (ICS) command messages to field device tags representing physical outputs, from a process that is not the recognized Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) or Distributed Control System (DCS) control application, targeting safety-critical output tags. OT operational-fidelity gate: Alert only when the action is not attributable to an authorized operator/engineering source for the specific target and function, and it is either outside an approved change/maintenance window or lacks matching change-control context; where telemetry permits, require corroborating device, configuration, or process-state effect. Suppress activity that fully matches approved maintenance, commissioning, failover, recovery, or tested control procedures.

patches.name: Analytic 1929
patches.description: Real-time monitoring identifies a loss of communication with serially-connected field devices correlated with a configuration change event on the serial-to-Ethernet gateway. Documented in the 2015 Ukraine attack, where Sandworm used malicious firmware to render serial-to-Ethernet converters inoperable. OT operational-fidelity gate: Alert only when the action is not attributable to an authorized operator/engineering source for the specific target and function, and it is either outside an approved change/maintenance window or lacks matching change-control context; where telemetry permits, require corroborating device, configuration, or process-state effect. Suppress activity that fully matches approved maintenance, commissioning, failover, recovery, or tested control procedures.

patches.name: Analytic 1933
patches.description: Real-time monitoring identifies an Industrial Control System (ICS) protocol restart/reset command directed at a field device from a source not in the approved engineering workstation list, particularly where multiple devices receive restart commands within a short window. Documented precedent: Industroyer exploited CVE-2015-5374 via a crafted 18-byte User Datagram Protocol (UDP) packet to port 50000 on Siemens SIPROTEC relays. OT operational-fidelity gate: Alert only when the action is not attributable to an authorized operator/engineering source for the specific target and function, and it is either outside an approved change/maintenance window or lacks matching change-control context; where telemetry permits, require corroborating device, configuration, or process-state effect. Suppress activity that fully matches approved maintenance, commissioning, failover, recovery, or tested control procedures.

patches.name: Analytic 1935
patches.description: Real-time monitoring identifies authentication to an external remote access gateway using credentials associated with Industrial Control System (ICS)-role accounts, from a source geolocation or Autonomous System Number (ASN) inconsistent with the account's established usage pattern, immediately followed by that session establishing connectivity into the ICS network zone. Documented in VPNFilter, which specifically targeted routers and network edge devices. OT operational-fidelity gate: Alert only when the account/device/session violates the approved identity + source host/jump path/zone policy and is corroborated by access to a protected OT asset, execution, configuration change, or another security-relevant follow-on event. Suppress approved shift activity, vendor support, break-glass use, commissioning, and documented remote-access windows.

patches.description: Real-time monitoring identifies an Industrial Control System (ICS) protocol message arriving at a device from a source whose identity is not in the approved communication baseline for that destination, where the message is structurally valid but originates outside the documented set of legitimate communicators. This technique-level analytic synthesizes Command Message (T1692.001) and Reporting Message (T1692.002). OT operational-fidelity gate: Alert only when the action is not attributable to an authorized operator/engineering source for the specific target and function, and it is either outside an approved change/maintenance window or lacks matching change-control context; where telemetry permits, require corroborating device, configuration, or process-state effect. Suppress activity that fully matches approved maintenance, commissioning, failover, recovery, or tested control procedures.

patches.name: Analytic 2047
patches.description: Real-time monitoring identifies the full firmware modification chain: a device entering firmware-update mode, receiving a large data transfer on a firmware-capable protocol port from a source not in the approved engineering workstation list, rebooting, and reporting a post-reboot firmware hash that does not match the authorized inventory. This technique-level analytic synthesizes System Firmware (T1693.001) and Module Firmware (T1693.002). OT operational-fidelity gate: Alert only when the action is not attributable to an authorized operator/engineering source for the specific target and function, and it is either outside an approved change/maintenance window or lacks matching change-control context; where telemetry permits, require corroborating device, configuration, or process-state effect. Suppress activity that fully matches approved maintenance, commissioning, failover, recovery, or tested control procedures.

patches.name: Analytic 2049
patches.description: Configured Windows object-access monitoring identifies a write to a Siemens project file by a process that is not the Siemens Totally Integrated Automation (TIA) Portal or Step7 engineering software, or by the legitimate Siemens tool immediately after loading a project from an untrusted path. Suppress activity that fully matches approved maintenance, commissioning, failover, recovery, or tested control procedures.

patches.name: Analytic 2066
patches.description: Real-time monitoring identifies a field device loading a modified autorun image (boot read-only memory, bootloader firmware) detected by a discrepancy between the device's declared firmware hash and the authorized firmware inventory hash, with post-reboot device behavior diverging from expected (unexpected protocols active, unanticipated network connections). OT operational-fidelity gate: Alert only when execution violates an approved signer/hash/path/parent/process or tool allowlist, or originates from an unauthorized user/tool, and is tied to an OT asset or follow-on OT-relevant action. Suppress vendor-signed software, approved engineering utilities, diagnostics, patching, backup, and documented maintenance.
